abstract_html: Assuming Pardon's Gromov–Witten evaluation for analytic families of threefolds, we lift the elementary-cluster expansion of Ionel and Parker to his rational algebra of one-cycles. For every smooth projective Calabi–Yau threefold the universal series factors uniquely with the elementary-cluster integers as exponents, indexed by effective classes in integral homology. We construct the genus-g factor using the volume-preserving circle in the torus that scales the two line summands of a balanced local curve. Symmetric functions of the two fiber projections isolate the multiples of the zero section and give compactly supported classes compatible with addition of cycles and multiplication by positive integers. Among series with these compatibilities, the local Gromov–Witten series of an elementary cluster determines the universal factor. Among split local Calabi–Yau curves with the antidiagonal action, agreement with the elementary cluster in degree two already forces the splitting degrees to be balanced.
